_: Pot material, per plant_id. The ONLY thing here that cannot be derived:
lineage, retirement and weights all come from the data, materials do not —
they live in whoever looked at the shelf. Guessing them cost a full
re-analysis on 2026-09-19 (the guess was 'the two largest and two smallest',
which was wrong), so they are written down instead.
Material is a property of the POT, not of the plant, so it is keyed by
plant_id and a repot ENDS one entry and starts another: cactus-05 and
cactus-05b are two different pots holding the same plant, and the material
does not carry across. Retired ids are kept for exactly that reason — their
historical readings still need the right material. cactus-05 is ceramic and
RETIRED (repotted into cactus-05b on 2026-08-30); cactus-05b is a different
pot and is plastic. Do not 'fix' that by moving the line to the live id.
Unlisted = plastic. Most pots are, and a new plastic pot should need no
edit here; only the exceptions are worth maintaining.
edit here; only the exceptions are worth maintaining.
Terracotta that is unglazed evaporates through its walls and will read as a
fast-drying pot for reasons that have nothing to do with the plant. If you
know a ceramic pot is glazed, say so — the two behave nothing alike.
